record.paper_title: Ten Open Problems in Grammatical Inference
record.original_question: Given a finite positive-negative sample ⟨X+, X−⟩ over a ranked alphabet and an integer k, can one decide in polynomial time whether the sample is k-acceptable, meaning that there exists a k-edge deterministic finite-state automaton consistent with all positive and negative examples? A k-edge deterministic finite-state automaton is a DFA-like model over a partially ordered alphabet whose outgoing transitions from each state are specified by at most k ordered symbol intervals, with distinct transition intervals from the same state disjoint.

evidence.quote: A ranked alphabet ⟨Σ, ≤⟩is an alphabet Σ with a relation ≤Σ which is a partial order (reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive) over Σ.
Definition 9. A sample ⟨X+, X−⟩is k-acceptable if there is a k-edge Dfa consistent with the data.
Problem 2. Given a sample ⟨X+, X−⟩, can we decide in polynomial time if a sample is k-acceptable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A ranked alphabet is a pair (Σ, ≤) where Σ is a finite alphabet and ≤ is a partial order on Σ. An interval of (Σ, ≤) is a subset of Σ of the form [a,b] = { c ∈ Σ : a ≤ c ≤ b }. A k-edge deterministic finite-state automaton over (Σ, ≤) is a tuple A = (Q, Σ, δ, q₀, F) where Q is a finite set of states, q₀ ∈ Q is the initial state, F ⊆ Q is the set of accepting states, and δ associates to each state q ∈ Q a set of at most k labeled transitions of the form (I, q′), where I is an interval of (Σ, ≤) and q′ ∈ Q, with the requirement that any two distinct intervals appearing on outgoing transitions from the same state are disjoint. A word w = a₁a₂…aₙ ∈ Σ* is accepted by A if there is a sequence of states q₀, q₁, …, qₙ with qₙ ∈ F such that for every i ∈ {1,…,n}, the state qᵢ₋₁ has an outgoing transition (Iᵢ, qᵢ) with aᵢ ∈ Iᵢ.

Sample. A sample is a pair ⟨X⁺, X⁻⟩ of finite disjoint subsets of Σ*. A k-edge DFA A is consistent with ⟨X⁺, X⁻⟩ if every word in X⁺ is accepted by A and no word in X⁻ is accepted by A. The sample ⟨X⁺, X⁻⟩ is k-acceptable if some k-edge DFA over (Σ, ≤) is consistent with it.

Problem. Given a finite ranked alphabet (Σ, ≤), a positive integer k, and a finite sample ⟨X⁺, X⁻⟩ over Σ, is there an algorithm that decides in time polynomial in the total size of the input (k, the description of (Σ, ≤), and the sample) whether ⟨X⁺, X⁻⟩ is k-acceptable?
artifact.status_search_result: The k-acceptability decision problem for k-edge DFAs over a ranked alphabet is listed as an open problem in the grammatical-inference open-problems literature. A web search did not turn up a published solution; related results address NP-hardness of producing minimal consistent DFAs and polynomial algorithms only under additional sample constraints, but none directly resolve polynomial decidability of k-acceptability for the k-edge DFA model defined here.

status_evidence.snippet: A sample ⟨X+,X−⟩ is k-acceptable if there is a k-edge DFA consistent with the data.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the definition and that polynomial-time decidability of k-acceptability is posed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Minimal consistent DFA from sample strings
status_evidence.snippet: Producing a minimal DFA consistent with a sample is NP-hard in general; polynomial algorithms exist only under constraints on the sample.
status_evidence.claim: Related hardness results suggest k-acceptability is non-trivial; no resolution of the specific k-edge DFA k-acceptability problem found.
